We need to solve a combinatorial game on a graph that initially has no odd cycles (i.e., it's bipartite). Players alternately add edges between non-adjacent vertices such that adding the edge does not create an odd cycle. The player who cannot move loses. Determine winner under optimal play.

We need to understand the game: We have a bipartite graph. Adding an edge between two vertices i and j is allowed if it does not create an odd cycle. Since graph is bipartite, adding an edge between two vertices in the same part of a connected component would create an odd cycle? Let's analyze.

In a bipartite graph, each connected component is bipartite. If we add an edge between two vertices in the same component, it will create an odd cycle if and only if they are in the same part of the bipartition? Actually, in a bipartite graph, all paths between two vertices have the same parity. If we add an edge between u and v, we create a cycle consisting of the new edge plus any path between u and v. The length of that cycle is 1 + length(path). If u and v are in the same part, all paths between them have even length, so cycle length = odd -> odd cycle.
